name: Visual Genome
description: Visual Genome is a dataset of 108,249 real-world images densely annotated with region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs. The dataset connects language and vision using crowdsourced dense image annotations and canonicalizes objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases to WordNet synsets.
creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bemstein, Li Fei-Fei
citeAs: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bemstein, Li Fei-Fei. Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332v1.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected and verified entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. The first release uses 108,249 images from the intersection of YFCC100M and MS-COCO. Data collection included multiple stages for region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs. Workers drew bounding boxes, wrote descriptions and QA pairs, extracted objects, attributes, and relationships from descriptions, and verified annotations.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis, User-generated content data
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some descriptions like "it is a sunny day" do not contain any objects and therefore have no region graphs associated with them.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The first release of the Visual Genome dataset uses 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets. These images are real-world, non-iconic images that were uploaded onto Flickr by users.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Scene graphs are created by combining region graphs for an image and merging co-referenced objects. Objects from different graphs are considered the same if their bounding boxes have overlap over union of 0.8, with worker confirmation before merging. Canonicalization maps objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases to WordNet synsets, using Stanford NLP tools, WordNet lexeme counts, hand-crafted mapping rules, and worker verification among five synset options.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Descriptions were filtered for diversity using BLEU score thresholds of 0.7 against previous image-specific descriptions and the top 100 most common global descriptions. Bounding boxes were required to satisfy coverage and quality constraints. Stanford dependency parsing was used to suggest nouns for object extraction. Attributes were normalized based on morphology, and relationships were processed by ignoring prepositions and matching WordNet sentence frames for verbs.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk annotated all components. For region descriptions, workers drew three bounding boxes and wrote three descriptions per image, with subsequent workers encouraged to write novel descriptions until 50 descriptions were collected per image. For objects, workers extracted objects from each description and grounded them with bounding boxes. For attributes and relationships, workers added attributes to objects and connected object pairs with relationships based on the description text. For QA pairs, workers wrote freeform and region-based question-answer pairs following rules to start with question words, avoid ambiguity and speculation, and ensure image-grounded answers. All data then went through verification using majority voting or rapid judgments.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All components except objects were verified using majority voting by three unique workers, and an annotation was added if at least two workers judged it factually correct. Objects were verified using rapid judgments. Canonicalization mappings were also sent to workers for verification, with workers choosing among five synset options without being told which was the proposed mapping.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Region descriptions: 50 per image collected, average of 42 per image retained; question-answer pairs: average of 17 per image; verification: 3 workers per annotation for majority voting
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers contributed. 93.02% were from the United States, 1.29% from the Philippines, 1.13% from Kenya, 0.94% from India, 0.50% from Russia, 0.47% from Canada, and 2.65% from other countries. The majority were between 25 and 34 years old; the youngest contributor was 18 and the oldest was 68. Gender split was 54.15% male and 45.85% female.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford dependency parser; Stanford NLP tools (CoreNLP); BLEU score computation for description diversity filtering
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Further visualizations, API, and additional information can be found online at visualgenome.org.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotator demographics including geographic location, age, and gender were collected and reported.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to enable training and benchmarking of the next generation of computer vision models for comprehensive scene understanding, including image search, question answering, and robotic interactions.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people. Certain sports such as skiing and surfing are overrepresented due to a bias in the image set. The paper also notes that previous datasets can bias workers toward easy, frequently occurring relationships, and Visual Genome was designed to reduce bias toward a particular task.
rai:dataLimitations: The canonicalization mappings are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. Relationships are difficult to classify due to high intra-class variability. Current captioning models trained on the dataset still have objectively low accuracy and are unable to reason about complex images. Some descriptions contain no explicit objects and therefore yield no region graphs.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a general-purpose representation of the visual world for training and benchmarking computer vision models. Use cases discussed include attribute prediction, relationship prediction, region description generation, visual question answering, dense image captioning, image understanding evaluation, relationship extraction, and semantic image retrieval.
